- **`live:P34.40` L2 status is the recorded seam** — P34.40's
  `lb-routes.sh` leg was QUEUED at 2026-10-08 and sits in RETURN PASS
  with `go = pre-authorised: GATE-B GB-Q4 (11A list; expires GATE-G4)`.
  GATE-G4 has sat — **that authorisation is expired**, and P34.40 is not
  on the GATE-G4 §4 19-row list. The contract's own words: the `/v1/*`
  step runs *"under that landed pre-authorisation **before** this roll,
  never skipped"* — with the authorisation expired, a still-paused L2
  is an operator naming at the next GATE (the byte-compare's API-served
  routes depend on it). The leg-runner checks the live URL map before
  anything runs, stopping if the rule is absent and unauthorised — the seam is
  recorded, not dropped. (For the web-only route set the comparison is
  honest either way: neither nginx config proxies `/v1/*`, so a route
  the flat edge 404s compares 404-after — measured, not asserted.)
- **Byte-identity composition** — genesis `conf/0` is an EMPTY promoted
  set (every gated namespace 404s, the same answer the flat site gives
  a not-published release route); `withdrawn.conf`/`selectors.conf`
  carry the floor's own `conf/` fragments VERBATIM (a deny map is never
  re-derived at cutover); deliberately **no** `releases/` index (the
  flat site 404s `/releases/` today — writing it would be the one
  visible change the leg forbids); the floor's `conf/` subtree
  (chrome/terms/renamed fragments + tombstone bodies) carries into
  `staged/conf/` where the template's globs and the internal
  `/conf/tombstone/` alias resolve them.
- **The retirement is a record, not a deletion** —
  `registry/serving.json` (`sig.serving-layout/1`,
  `legacy_publish_class: "retired"`) is what `sig-ops publish-web
  --apply` refuses on; the `sig-web` bucket itself is never modified —
  public-read IAM intact, root bytes the 90-day floor source.
- **Rollback is a traffic move, never a re-versioned edit** — the
  prior revision keeps running; on any byte difference the leg moves
  traffic back to it, restoring image + env + mounts wholesale (RR-7's
  no-traffic-reversion rule governs *release* rollbacks; the cutover's
  restore is to the still-live prior revision — the recorded digest is
  the same object either way).

## Phase 1 — implementation

- **`ops/src/ops/release_reversal.py`** (+~400) — the cutover's
  registry half, riding the landed floor machinery:
  - `SERVING_SCHEMA = "sig.serving-layout/1"`, `SERVING_OBJECT =
    "registry/serving.json"`, `serving_layout(store)` — the serving-layout
    record readers.
  - `compose_floor_generation(store, label, floor, go_ref, now)` — the
    genesis `conf/0` object set: `latest.json` (LATEST_SCHEMA_V2,
    `publication_id: None`, `legacy_floor: <label>`, `conf_gen: 0`,
    `cutover: true` — a floor pointer, never a pub id); empty
    `promoted.map`; `withdrawn.conf`/`selectors.conf` carried verbatim
    from the floor's `conf/withdrawn_*`/`conf/selectors*` fragments (or
    the generation's empty placeholders when the floor has none);
    `labels.conf` from the label map; **no `releases/` set**.
  - `_floor_fragment_names` — every floor `conf/` object → mirrored
    `staged/conf/` carry (nested `tombstone/` dirs land verbatim).
  - `verb_cutover` — refuses a non-`legacy-<YYYYMMDD>` label
    (`bad-floor-label`), an unimported floor (`unknown-floor`), a
    recorded-but-unstaged floor (`floor-unstaged`), a registry past
    genesis (`genesis-passed` — a second floor-serve is `release
    rollback --to <label>`'s act), a non-digest `--web-image`
    (`image-not-digest`), and a non-`sig.withdrawal-registry/*`
    `--withdrawals` seed (`bad-input`). `--apply` requires the
    `registry/authorities/` go record (checked, never created). Under
    the registry lock: `conf/0` create-if-absent → the `staged/conf/`
    carry → the withdrawals seed (verbatim or absent — the carried
    barrier is the truth either way) → `serving.json` → six post-checks
    (`conf0.latest`, `conf0.promoted-map-empty`, `conf0.withdrawn`,
    `conf0.selectors`, `conf0.no-releases-index`, `serving.retired`) →
    a `failed` event + refusal on any fail, else the `legacy-cutover`
    journal event recording the roll intent (env
    `SIG_CONF_GEN=0`/`SIG_LATEST_PUB`/`SIG_LATEST_LABEL`/`SIG_STAGING=0`,
    mount, min-instances) verbatim. Idempotent under create-if-absent.
- **`ops/src/ops/release_pipeline.py`** (+18) — `run_verb` dispatches
  `cutover` → `verb_cutover` with the parser's flags.
- **`ops/src/ops/cli.py`** (+66) — `sig-ops release cutover` parser
  (`--label`/`--go`/`--web-image`/`--min-instances`/`--withdrawals`/
  `--service`/`--release-bucket`/`--mount-path`/`--project`/`--region`);
  `publish-web` gains `--release-registry` (default
  `SIG_RELEASE_REGISTRY`) feeding the retirement guard.
- **`ops/src/ops/publish.py`** (+60) — the retirement guard, the
  SIG-OPS-004/SIG-REL-004 enforcement completing: `run_publish_web`
  reads `registry/serving.json` (via `release_registry`) **before any
  write or sync** and `--apply` refuses when it declares
  `legacy_publish_class: "retired"` — naming layout/floor/cutover_at in
  the refusal. Three honest states: no record = the legacy path is
  still live; an un-openable registry = `_unevaluated` recorded in the
  result (the guard refuses only a record it read); a retired record =
  refusal. Dry-run reports the state, never refuses on it.
- **`ops/gcp/web-cutover.sh`** (new, ~360 lines) — the leg-runner:
  window guard (exit 42 outside weekday 14:00–20:00Z; the never band
  03:00–06:30Z reported in the same message) → per-leg `--apply`
  (`prestate`/`import`/`compose`/`roll`/`poststate`/`rollback`, or
  `all`) → AR-2 prestate (`run services describe`, `url-maps export`,
  canonical + run.app `route-compare capture`, a read-only rsync
  snapshot of the then-current tree + sha256 manifest with object/byte
  counts) → `release import-floor --apply` → `release cutover --apply`
  → `web.sh --apply image` + `run deploy` with the release mount and
  the recorded env (`SIG_LATEST_PUB=legacy-<date>`, `SIG_CONF_GEN=0`,
  `SIG_STAGING=0`, `SIG_LATEST_LABEL`) — the mounts are read back
  and replaced (never guessed) → `route-compare verify` on BOTH
  origins → on failure the recorded rollback (traffic move to the
  still-running prior revision) is printed verbatim. `SIG_CUTOVER_GO`
  names the operator's authorities record; `--check` prints the whole
  plan with no ADC.
- **`docs/ops/RUNBOOK.md`** §13 — the cutover procedure + the
  retirement declaration, runbook-checked (63 command lines verified).
- **`docs/build/tools/record_policy/return_pass.toml`** — the
  `P35.59` leg row (`P35.59-dark-cutover`: queued disposition, OM-20
  listing verbatim, both still-unmet live prerequisites, the verbatim
  re-run prompt) rides the **closeout** commit, not the impl commit —
  a `returnPass:` id counts as landed for `nextTicket` (V2
  `next-not-lowest`), so the row lands only with the BUILD_INDEX row +
  nextTicket advance (the `59817162`/P35.41 convention; a placeholder
  comment marks the spot). The `live:` edges are already recorded:
  `P34.40-lb-routes` and `P35.53-release-infra` list P35.59 in
  `live_dependants`.

- **Disposition:** QUEUED — never run, never claimed run.
- **Exact command:**

  (or per-leg: `--apply prestate|import|compose|roll|poststate`; the
  verbatim ticket re-run prompt is
  `implement-spec spec=docs/tickets/336_P35.59__dark-cutover-to-release-layout.md live_verification=true`).
- **Window (AR-3):** the next preferred weekday 14:00–20:00Z slot —
  **Monday 2026-10-26T14:00Z** at the earliest — never 03:00–06:30Z.
- **Preconditions, in order:**
  1. `live:P35.53` — the release-infra leg applied (the private
     `…-sig-release` bucket + `sig-release-rt` exist; D-P35.53-1).
  2. `live:P34.40` L2 — `gcloud compute url-maps export` shows the
     `/v1`,`/v1/*` path rule (the byte-compare's API routes depend on
     it). GB-Q4 expired at GATE-G4 and P34.40 is not on the §4 list —
     a still-paused L2 is an operator naming at the next GATE before
     this leg, never skipped and never run under expired authority.
  3. AR-2 restore point — `--apply prestate` captures the service spec
     (revision + digest + env + mounts), the URL-map export, the
     both-origin route baselines and the then-current tree's sha256
     manifest captured before any write.
  4. `SIG_CUTOVER_GO` names a `registry/authorities/` record the
     operator placed (the OM-20 listing — checked, never created).
- **Sequence at the leg (fail-closed):** AR-2 → floor import
  (`staged/v/legacy-<YYYYMMDD>/` + object/byte manifest — a floor
  label, never a pub id) → `conf/0` + staged/conf carry +
  `serving.json` retirement → `sig-web` roll by pinned digest
  (min-instances 1, `…-sig-release` at `/mnt/rel`) → `route-compare
  verify` on canonical + run.app. **Any byte difference fails the leg;
  the rollback is the recorded traffic move to the still-running prior
  revision** — image, env and mounts restored wholesale, never patched.
- **The landing `date -u` is written at completion** — D-R11-LATER-20's
  90-day clock anchors on it (and `serving.json`'s `cutover_at`). The
  `sig-web` bucket keeps its public-read IAM and root bytes meanwhile;
